> `crates/db/src/live.rs`: `Shipper` (the owner's chain, credit, retained tail and durable position), `Replica` (a
> holder's fence and head, guard-then-apply), `adopt` (phase one's choice), and the entry, install and reply
> encodings with hostile-input tests. `crates/db/tests/live.rs` runs it under a nemesis (loss, duplication,
> reordering, partitions, holder crashes, owner loss with takeover, a superseded owner shipping on, holders that learn
> a takeover late) for 200 seeds × 3,000 steps at f=1 and f=2, checking Agreement, NoLoss and StaleNeverCommits after
> every step and Convergence after healing. All held, with 110 and 241 takeovers, 231 and 416 installs, 2,020 and 5,431
> stale-epoch refusals, and 4,600 and 2,871 durable positions. Red-checked by mutation: adopting the lowest-ranked
> report fails NoLoss at once, and removing both the fence and the owner check fails StaleNeverCommits. The
> stale-refusal counter found one defect before any history check did: a holder refused a superseded owner as
> unauthorized before checking its fence, so that owner never learned it was fenced and shipped on. The fence is now
> checked first.
>
> **Holders follow the candidates (2026-11-07, A-200's amendment of that date).** The shipper's holder set changes by a
> joint transition (`Shipper::begin_transition`, `transferred`, `activate`); the daemon begins one whenever the
> configuration names other candidates for the volume (`fleet.live.holders_transition`) and switches once the new set
> holds every durable write (`fleet.live.holders_activated`). The model runs the same nemesis over `4f + 1` hosts with
> the configuration naming random candidate sets: 0 of 400 seeds broken, 3,622 activations, 599 of them keeping fewer
> than `f` of the old holders.
>
> **On the transport (2026-11-04).** `crates/cluster/src/live.rs`: `ship` sends an entry or install to each holder
> over its warm session (kinds 22 and 23) and folds the replies until the write is durable, through the
> wake-on-reply collector; `serve_entry` and `serve_install` are the holder's answer. Measured over real loopback
> endpoints with the daemon's derived runtime (`replication_bench`; BENCHMARKS "Live shipping over the transport"): a
> 64-byte write durable on two hosts in 16.6–20.3 µs at the median and 28.7–32.5 µs at p99, a 4 KiB write in
> 22.6–27.2 µs and 37.9–71.8 µs, a 64 KiB write in 108–149 µs and 160–292 µs; unchanged with one holder dead. A test
> over the simulated fabric (`crates/cluster/tests/live.rs`) found that `ship` sent nothing when its position was
> already durable, so the owner's period never caught a holder up; it always sends now, and a late holder is
> installed once and then follows. Owed: the daemon's publications shipped through it, with barriers answered at
> durability and phase one in the takeover round; real-process chaos.
>
> **In the daemon, slice one (2026-11-05): the owner ships and the candidates keep.** `crates/server/src/live_ship.rs`.
> Each publication of a live-shipped volume that commits (`publish_shard`) is appended on the volume's own shard, so
> positions follow publication order inside the barrier; its payload is the record the journal took (or the whole
> image after a checkpoint) and the content of every extent it names, read through `Volume::read` and sealed under
> the lineage key. A task of that shard sends what each candidate lacks over the control shard's sessions
> (`slates_cluster::live::exchange`) and folds the replies there. Candidates check chain and fence, keep the sealed
> entries since the last whole one within twice the volume's size, and answer with their head (record kinds 22, 23).
> A publication that cannot become an entry (the credit full, a read or seal refused) leaves the volume owing a whole
> record, which the next publication or the record period appends. `status` reports each live log
> (`shard N live shipping|held VOLUME head= durable= owed= epoch= identity= fence=`: since 2026-11-06 the head's epoch
> and chain identity and the copy's fence too, so a chaos run checks Agreement and fencing from outside the processes,
> `crates/cli/tests/live_chaos.rs`). Across three real daemon processes
> (`crates/cli/tests/live_fleet.rs`, `SLATES_TEST_CLI=1`), five writes end with the owner durable at its head, nothing
> owed and both candidates at that head, 4 of 4 runs. Two defects that run found are fixed in the slice: a refusal was
> re-shipped at once, so a holder that did not hold the volume's catalog yet looped with its owner (982 and 5,501
> refusals in one five-write run, 0 to 20 after); and a burst that outran the credit left its last writes unshipped
> until another write came.
>
> **Slice two (2026-11-05): barriers wait for durability.** A recorded verb that changes a live-shipped volume commits
> its effects, then neither records its completion nor answers until its publication's position is durable
> (`live_ship::durable_target`, `defer`, `resolve`; a retry joins the wait, `live_ship::join`), as a green's submit
> waits for its merge record; a stable NFS `WRITE` or `COMMIT` waits after its barrier (`nfs::stable_once_durable`), at
> most the daemon's liveness budget, then answers `NFS3ERR_JUKEBOX` and never a stability it does not have. Holders
> that never answer make writers wait: backpressure, never a false success. Across three real daemon processes
> (`crates/cli/tests/live_fleet.rs`): five `slates write`s each deferred (`fleet.live.awaited` 5), the owner's log
> durable at its head with nothing owed the moment the last returns; five `FILE_SYNC` NFS writes each waited
> (`fleet.live.resolved`), the log durable at each write's own position right after its reply (1, 2, 3, 4, 5), none
> late. Red-checked: with the control-verb wait removed the last write returned at head 1, durable none, owed
> (3 of 3); with the NFS wait removed the counter is zero and the race shows an undurable reply in 2 of 3.
>
> **A clone of a live volume is answered once its own log holds it (2026-11-19, A-577).** A clone of a live-shipped
> volume is live-shipped too, and its `Clone` answered on its origin's log, which the clone did not change; its record,
> a copy of its origin's, named the origin's head, so nothing of it shipped until its own first seal; and its log's
> whole records were its recovery image, which names its inherited tree by number, so a successor with no origin found
> no root to lay out. Now a clone's registers start at the creation head, a live log's whole records stand alone (every
> inode, content and all), its reply waits for its own first whole entry durable on `f` holders (on the cross-partition
> path too, after its alias), and its status reports the window its seals leave until its new log has answered at a
> whole entry. A-577's entry measures the cost: one entry, the clone's whole image, one round trip.
>
> **The held replies' bound is met before a verb runs (2026-11-18).** A shard holds at most `awaiting_bound` such
> replies (its client seats times ring slots). A recorded verb that could be held (one that changes a live-shipped
> volume, or a destroy while `f > 0`) meets that bound before it runs (`live_ship::refuse_over_bound`, from
> `verbs::run_recorded`): refused `Overloaded`, it changed nothing, and its resend under the same id runs it once, as on
> a plain volume. Before, the bound was met in `defer`, after the verb's effects had committed with no completion
> record, so the resend ran the verb again over them: a directory's resend was refused `AlreadyExists`, an append landed
> twice (g232's finding). Held by
> `a_live_shipped_verb_refused_at_the_held_reply_bound_changed_nothing_so_its_resend_runs_once`
> (`crates/server/tests/fleet.rs`). An asynchronous outcome that may wait so (a mapped file's write-back, a checkout)
> takes a seat among the held replies as its task begins (`live_ship::take_seat`), refused `Overloaded` at the bound
> before it writes anything; its wait fills the seat (`defer`, which no longer refuses for room), or it gives the seat
> back when it completes without one (`release_seat`). A map's release lets its copy go whatever its write-back
> answers, so it is seated when there is room and never refused for room (`seat_if_room`). An outcome that began with no
> seat (that release, or one whose volume turned live-shipped while it ran) is held past the bound, counted
> (`fleet.live.held_past_bound`), rather than refused after its commit. Held by `a_live_shipped_maps_sync_refused_at_the_held_reply_bound_wrote_nothing`: before, the sync was
> refused `Overloaded` with its stores already in the file.
>
> **Slice three (2026-11-05): takeover from the live log.** The whole-state kind (23) carries a successor's fetch beside
> installs, by tag (`slates_db::live::Fetch`). A takeover that adopts a live-shipped volume's head runs phase one for
> its log (`live_ship::fetch`): every candidate of the head's placement raises its fence to the head's placed epoch,
> takes the successor as owner, and answers with its head and the sealed entries it keeps; the greatest head among at
> least `f + 1` answers is adopted (`slates_db::live::adopt`). Whole entries carry the volume's lineage key wrapped for
> each neighbour (the `sealing` a head carries), so the successor opens the log whether or not the volume ever sealed;
> it replays the whole image and the deltas after it (`VolumeImage::apply`) and serves the volume as an archive of
> that image and the content runs (`live_ship::Rebuilding`, the export's layout; in turns since A-374), through the
> same restore and making a seal's takeover uses (`verbs::restore_taken_over`, `materialize_taken_over_restored`). A log that cannot be rebuilt whole is refused, counted
> (`fleet.live.takeover_refused`), never silently replaced by an older seal. The successor keeps the volume
> live-shipped (its catalog carries the flag) and ships under the head's epoch, above the dead owner's. Across three
> real daemon processes (`a_live_volumes_acknowledged_writes_survive_its_owners_death`): five writes, each answered at
> durability, no snapshot ever taken, the owner killed with SIGKILL; a survivor serves all five files byte for byte
> after 2.27, 2.05, 1.85 and 1.83 s (4 of 4). Red-checked: with the live log not read, the successor serves the volume
> empty (every file `NotFound`), the loss the log closes. Found on the way and closed in the same slice: a volume whose
> owner died before its creation head was placed at `f + 1` (the record period, up to 100 ms) was unknown to any
> takeover, so writes it had acknowledged were lost with it (2 of 2 runs killed right after the writes served nothing,
> `OwnerUnreachable`). A live write now waits for its volume's head placement as well as its own durability
> (`live_ship::head_placed`; `fleet::record_acks_in` answers the waits it completes), and the flow kills the owner the
> moment the last write returns: served whole in 1.93, 1.93 and 2.17 s (3 of 3). Also owed: FUSE `fsync`, a
> candidate's copy across its own daemon's restart, hard links (an archive carries each name as its own file), and
> extended attributes in the rebuilt volume.
>
> **Chaos across real processes (2026-11-05).** SIGSTOP is the unprivileged partition (a stopped daemon answers
> nothing and keeps its ports; SIGCONT returns it with every timer late, as a healed partition or a long stall does);
> netem and network namespaces need privileges this project never takes. `crates/cli/tests/live_fleet.rs`:
> - *A candidate partitioned away, then healed*: writes stay durable through the other candidate (client-seen 3–16 ms
>   but the first, about 103 ms, the session finding the stopped peer), the log durable at its head when the last
>   returns; the healed candidate catches up to the owner's head within about 1–2 s (4 of 4).
> - *Latency injected*: both candidates stopped 30 ms of every 60 ms, out of phase, so for 15 ms of each both are
>   stopped: 30 writes, client-seen p50 3.0–3.8 ms, p90 32.6–33.6 ms, max 35.1–47.4 ms, every one durable at its return,
>   none refused for room, both candidates at the owner's head afterwards.
> The partition found a defect: a live exchange's deadline came from the consensus round's budget, which is derived
> from the slowest path's tail, and a stopped peer inflates it, so one exchange held the peer's only session past a
> 40 s wait and the healed candidate never caught up (1 of 2 runs at first; 0 of 8 since). Live exchanges now run under
> the daemon's liveness budget (`fleet::live_budget`), and an exchange no holder answered drops that link to be dialed
> afresh (`live_ship::lose_links`), as an unanswered discovery exchange does.
>
> **Chaos, continued (2026-11-05).** Three more flows, and two more defects they found:
> - *A superseded owner resumed*: the owner stopped until the survivors took the volume over (served whole after
>   1.8–2.1 s), two more writes made on the successor, then the old owner resumed and a write tried through it: never
>   acknowledged within the 40 s wait, never on the successor (`a_superseded_owner_resumed_after_its_takeover_is_fenced`).
>   The first run of it hung on the successor's own first write: a holder off the new chain was offered entries from
>   its last on-chain head, which it refused, forever, because the shipper's `pending` did not know the holder was owed
>   an install. The model, driven as the daemon drives it (re-ship only what `pending` says), failed Convergence the
>   same way; `Shipper` now remembers holders owed an install, the model passes again (f=1: 309 installs, f=2: 455).
>   And an install at a checkpoint a holder already holds is refreshed by a new whole record, which may go one entry
>   past the credit (`Shipper::append_checkpoint`): with both candidates behind, waiting for credit no laggard could
>   free deadlocked the stall flow. (Since 2026-11-07 the refresh is an image beside the log while the log itself is
>   whole; the whole record past the credit remains for a log that lost a change, as with both candidates behind. See
>   "An install image beside the log" below.)
> - *Clients cut off mid-write*: ten writers SIGKILLed right after starting, between finished writes: the log whole on
>   every candidate, every deferred reply resolved (awaited 10, resolved 10).
> - *A live volume destroyed*: its candidates let their copy of its log go once the tombstone reaches them
>   (`live_ship::let_go`); before, they kept it forever (red without the release, 1 of 1).
> All eight flows pass together in 55 s.
>
> **The tail and three more defects (2026-11-05).** All nine process flows pass together in 4.1–4.2 s (twice), each
> flow's fleet in its own directory: one directory per test process had let parallel fleets overwrite each other's
> manifest, and eight of nine daemons were handed another fleet's ports.
> - *The rare 100 ms write*: two causes, each a wait for the record period. A send that found its holder's session lent
>   was dropped (`borrow_session` now waits for it, within the liveness budget). A write the credit turned away waited
>   for the next write or the period to append the whole record it owed (the reply that frees the credit now appends
>   it). The worst live stable write went from 86–276 ms to 0.47–1.87 ms (BENCHMARKS "The 100 ms tail").
> - *A superseded owner was never told*: after the takeover the configuration names the successor, so a holder refused
>   the old owner's entries `Unauthorized` before it reached the fence. The old owner could not tell that from a
>   passing refusal and held the write unanswered for the whole 40 s wait. A holder now answers a message below the fence
>   its copy promised `StaleEpoch` (`not_served`, read from the header by `live::epoch_of`). The owner keeps the
>   volume marked fenced: it refuses every write waiting on it and every later one `StaleEpoch`, and a parked stable NFS
>   write answers "try again", never "durable". Before, the fence dropped the shipper, and a parked reply read "no
>   shipper" as nothing to wait for. The flow now requires the refusal: the stale write exits 1 at once, and the flow
>   takes 3.9 s instead of 43 s.
> - *A destroyed volume's shipper was kept on its owner*, with a whole copy of the volume (`live_ship::forget` at the
>   teardown's end and in the orphan sweep: waiting verbs refused `NotFound`, parked replies woken to "not durable").
>   The destroy flow now holds the owner to it too (red first, 1 of 1).
>
> **The round, counted hop by hop (2026-11-18, g076b).** A-200's measurement placed the added median in "the
> cross-shard dispatch round" from averages (an entry's build 13.3 µs, its round 90.7 µs, the exchange alone about
> 25 µs) and owed the round's hops apart. The owner now times each write's round from stamps on the host's one monotonic
> clock (`slates_machine::clock`, one origin across shards and processes; a shard's driver clock starts at its own epoch,
> so its readings on two shards differ by a constant and a span across them is not a span): the publication reaching
> the shipper, its message made, its lane free on the control shard, the message sent and its answer read there
> (`live_ship::LaneStamps`), and the fold that makes the entry durable. Each pair of consecutive stamps is one hop,
> counted with its nanoseconds once a write by that fold (`fleet.live.hop.{build,to_control,lane,exchange,to_owner,round}`
> and each `_ns`; `count_hops`), so the five hops add up to the round exactly. A reply held for the entry times its own
> wake from the fold (`fleet.live.hop.reply`, `wait_durable`), and a holder times its serve, the publication that keeps
> the entry included (`fleet.live.hop.holder`). Held by `a_live_writes_round_is_counted_hop_by_hop_and_the_hops_add_up_to_it`
> (`crates/server/tests/fleet.rs`: 16 writes in a closed loop; each hop timed once a timed round; the hops' nanoseconds
> equal to the rounds'). The breakdown under the contract command is owed (the supervisor's run).
>
> **A live write parks no shard on its path where a held shard polls (2026-11-18, A-396, g076b).** The round's cost was
> parked threads, not the cross-shard hop: each shard on a write's path (the owner awaiting the fold, its control shard
> awaiting the dispatch and then the holder's answer, the holder awaiting the entry) slept in its driver between its
> parts and paid a wake. Each now asks to hold its idle window across its wait (`crate::live_hold`): the owner while a
> reply waits for durability, for the volume's answer window (`hold_for_answer`, from `done_or_park` and `defer`); the
> control shard through an exchange, for that holder's (`hold_for_exchange`), and after a dispatch, for its stream's
> next; a holder after it answers an entry, for the owner's next (`serve_taken`). Every window is learned from the
> traffic it waits on by RFC 9002 §5.3's law, a stream's never longer than its run (A-326's rule), and each shard keeps a
> hold only while its measured idle turn is shorter than its wake (A-387's predicate, the runtime's own decision on
> every host: a macOS shard, whose `kevent` naps, declines). Counted `fleet.live.hold.{answer,exchange,dispatches,
> entries}` (asked) and `fleet.live.hold.declined`; held by
> `a_live_write_loop_asks_the_owners_the_control_shards_and_the_holders_shards_to_hold`. Prototype and first A/B figures
> in A-396. Landed before its A/B under Ada's rule of 2026-11-18 (an agent implements, unit-tests, merges and ends): the
> supervisor's A/B, main before the holds against main with them, decides whether they stay.
>
> **FUSE `fsync` at durability (2026-11-05).** A FUSE mount answered `fsync` at the owner's own barrier, so on a
> live-shipped volume it claimed what no candidate held: with both candidates' processes stopped it returned success in
> 19 µs (`a_fuse_fsync_on_a_live_volume_answers_only_once_a_candidate_holds_it`, red first). An `fsync` (or `fsyncdir`)
> whose barrier published a live volume not yet durable is now held on its mount (`fuse::hold_fsync`), and the mount's
> task serves the kernel's other requests meanwhile. FUSE answers a request out of order, and an `fsync` reply grants the
> kernel nothing, so the held reply is sent from its own bytes. The task answers it once the log is durable where the
> barrier put it, or `EIO` once the liveness budget has passed or the volume is destroyed or its owner superseded
> (`fuse::settle_held`; the check is `live_ship::durability`, which the NFS wait now uses too). Unlike `crate::told`'s
> wait it cannot deadlock: it waits on candidates over the network, never on another mount's kernel lock. Held replies
> are bounded per mount by the shard's bound on held verbs; past it an `fsync` is answered `EIO`, counted. Measured in
> the flow: with both candidates stopped the `fsync` fails `EIO` after 1.0006 s (the liveness budget); healthy and after
> the candidates resume, it succeeds.
>
> **The wait is judged by what it hears, not by the clock (A-292; found 2026-11-09, on main 2026-11-17).** A held
> `fsync` gave up at one wall-clock deadline of the liveness budget from its hold, so load that slowed the candidates or
> the owner spent it: a healthy `fsync` answered `EIO` 1 in 6 runs on main and 2 in 9 on raft-7 at load 36–145. Under load
> on adacachy2 its bytes were already held by a candidate while the volume's head placement, shipped on the membership
> loop, was still in flight. Now each live volume counts the acknowledgements that moved its durability forward
> (`live_ship::LiveVolume::heard`: a holder's acknowledged position advancing, its head's or catalog's placement gaining
> an acknowledgement), and a held reply waits in windows of the liveness budget. A window that ends with that count
> moved starts the next. One that ends with nothing heard gives up, but only once the owner has read what its
> candidates sent before it ended: the daemon's control shard, which holds the sessions every acknowledgement arrives
> on and hands each to the volume's shard as a task there, must have waited in its driver twice since the silence was
> seen, and the verdict is given at a look after the one that saw it, the looks a heartbeat apart (`live_ship::heard_now`,
> `DURABLE_LOOK_NS`). A shard waits only when nothing is ready to run, and each wait collects everything readable, so two
> waits after a moment mean everything that reached it before then has been read and handed on. Without that step the
> first look after a window's end judged it, so an owner kept off its CPU across that end could take its own deafness
> for its candidates' silence (raft's failing run showed the owner itself 600 ms late). The wait ends at its total bound
> whatever it hears: the failover SLO from the hold (10 s by default), the operator's bound on how long an owner's object
> may go unserved before a takeover serves it, past which a write not yet durable is past what the fleet promises to
> keep. Without it a wait that keeps hearing other writes' progress while its own position is never acknowledged, or
> whose receiver never waits, would not end (banned item 8); it is kept on the clock, not as a count of windows, since a
> window whose silence awaits its receiver lasts longer than a window. The rule is one pure module every transport
> judges by (`slates_bridge_core::durable_bound`): the FUSE `fsync` (`fuse::settle_held`), the shared wait of an NFS
> stable write or `COMMIT` and a Shards `FSYNC` (`live_ship::wait_durable`), the virtio-fs device's `FSYNC`
> (`slates_bridge_virtiofs`'s device, its wait begun and judged through `BridgeAccess::durable_bound` and
> `durable_heard`), which had kept a single deadline of its own, and WinFsp's held flush (`winfsp::settle_held`), which
> had too. Stopped candidates acknowledge nothing and are given up a window and two or three looks after the hold (1.2 to
> 1.3 s by construction, where it was one window); candidates that answer slowly keep the wait going. A refusal logs what
> durability still lacked and which rule ended the wait (`live_ship::durability_report`). Red first: with both
> candidates cycling stopped 700 ms and running 100 ms, `a_fuse_fsync_on_a_live_volume_waits_out_candidates_that_answer_slowly`
> refused the first `fsync` `EIO` after 1.0013–1.0037 s, 3 of 3; after, 6 of 6 succeeded in 1.50–1.59 s (adacachy2,
> 2026-11-09). A guest's `FSYNC` whose volume hears an acknowledgement every half window is answered `0` after a window
> and a half (`a_guests_fsync_of_a_live_volume_waits_while_its_volume_keeps_progressing`), and one whose receiver holds
> its acknowledgement unread until half a window past the window's end is answered `0`, never `EIO`
> (`a_guests_fsync_is_not_refused_while_its_receiver_has_not_read_what_came`); each was answered `EIO` at one window by
> the rule before it (`docs/bugs/2026-11-09-a-healthy-live-fsync-was-refused-at-a-wall-clock-deadline.md`).
>
> **Silence is the holders' only when they were asked (A-301, 2026-11-17).** The receiver's two waits prove the owner
> has read what came, not that it asked. Some of what a held reply waits for is asked only at the owner's own pace: a
> fresh volume's head and catalog are shipped by the coordinator's period after that period's other rounds, each
> awaited in turn (`fleet::ship_shard_heads`), so a period a loaded machine stretches past a window left a window in
> which nothing was asked and nothing heard, and the wait gave up on holders that had never been asked. Each live volume
> now keeps when its owner first asked a holder something since it last heard anything on the volume's durability path
> (`live_ship::LiveVolume::unanswered_since_ns`): a lane opened to send it entries or an install (`live_ship::dispatch`),
> or a head's or catalog's placement round sent (`fleet::ship_head`, noted on the volume's shard before the round, which
> that shard runs before the round's acknowledgements). Anything heard clears it. A window that ended with nothing heard
> is confirmed only once that ask is a window old, a holder having had the whole liveness budget to answer it, and then
> by the receiver's two waits as before; an owner that never asks holds the verdict only to the total bound. The rule
> never gives up earlier than before; with candidates stopped, the barrier's lanes are the ask, so the refusal still
> comes a window and two or three looks after the hold. A give-up's record names the oldest unanswered ask's age
> (`live_ship::durability_report`). Red first: the rule's
> `a_window_in_which_the_owner_asked_nothing_is_given_up_only_once_its_ask_is_a_window_old` and
> `an_owner_that_never_asks_holds_the_verdict_only_to_the_total_bound`, and the device's
> `a_guests_fsync_is_not_refused_while_its_owner_has_asked_its_holders_nothing` (an owner that asks half a window past
> the window's end, answered at once), each given up `Silent` (`EIO`) by A-292's rule alone before the owner had asked.
> Not tracked as an ask: a pair key's delivery (one per owner shard and candidate, not per volume), so a wait on it
> alone holds to the total bound; and the ask is kept per volume, not per holder, so a stopped candidate's re-sent lane
> can stand in for an ask the owner has not yet made of a live one (a stopped candidate and a stretched period at once,
> where the rule is A-292's alone).
>
> **A held verb's reply ends at the failover SLO (A-354, 2026-11-18; g230).** A verb of the slates protocol whose
> reply waits for its volume's log (`live_ship::defer`) or for its destroy's tombstone (`live_ship::defer_destroy`) was
> answered only once durable, fenced or destroyed: every transport judges its own held reply by the rule above, and
> this, its own holder, by none. So a log that could never be held kept its writer waiting as long as its daemon lived:
> A-353's successor, whose holders' catalog was refused for good, held a write 21 minutes (g229's capture, 2026-11-18).
> Each held reply now keeps when it was held and is refused at the rule's total bound, the failover SLO from its hold
> (read from the rule's own spans, `live_ship::durable_spans`, so it is the transports' bound and follows the failover
> estimate wherever it is published, never a number of its own):
> judged at the period's visit to its volume (`live_ship::judge_held`), a destroy's once a period on its shard
> (`live_ship::judge_held_destroys`), answered `Refusal::DurabilityPending { held_ns }` and counted
> `fleet.live.held_gave_up` (`fleet.destroy.held_gave_up`), with what durability lacked logged. Through a shorter
> silence the writer still waits, as the 2026-11-05 sweep chose (a writer waits, never a false success), so a candidate
> stopped for a few liveness budgets still answers the write when it resumes. The refusal is recorded as the request's
> completion, as a fence's is, so a retry under the same id meets it (§4.9); the verb's effects stay committed on the
> owner, never claimed durable, and a consumer runs the verb again under a new id (slates-api's
> `RetryCause::DurabilityPending`, CONTRACT 22). A retry that joined a request's wait is answered with it, judged by the
> request's first hold. Held by
> `a_reply_held_for_a_durability_it_cannot_reach_is_refused_at_the_failover_delay_and_runs_again`
> (`crates/server/tests/fleet.rs`: both survivors refuse the owner's register records, so a new live volume's head never
> places; the write refused after 10.03 and 10.08 s, the same request answered the same refusal, and the write sent again
> answered `FsDone` once the refusals lifted).
>
> **Every other durability claim (2026-11-05, the sibling sweep of FUSE `fsync`).** Each place a client is told data is
> durable on a live volume now waits for the position its barrier published, and the same failing test holds each to
> it across three real daemon processes (`crates/cli/tests/live_fleet.rs`): with both candidates' processes stopped
> the claim fails or waits, never succeeds; healthy and after they resume, it succeeds.
> - *A Shards stream's `FSYNC`* (`crate::shards`; its DAX compare-back runs before it): answered `0` in 337 µs with
>   both candidates stopped, red first; now held until durable, `EIO` after 1.0011–1.0025 s (3 of 3).
> - *A writable map's `MapSync`* and a writable `ReleaseMap` (`crate::direct_map`): a deferred verb, which the recorded
>   verb's wait passed over, answered `MapSynced` in 683 µs with the log durable at none; now completed through
>   `live_ship::defer`, so it waits as `slates write` does: unanswered through three liveness budgets stopped,
>   answered at once after the resume with the log durable at its head (3 of 3).
> - *A green's `checkout`* into its live base (`crate::checkout`, `image::complete_once_durable`): answered `CheckedOut`
>   with both stopped, red first; now waits the same way (3 of 3).
> - *NFSv4 `COMMIT` and stable `WRITE`* need no change: the v4 front end serves each through the v3 procedure
>   (`RoutedBackend::call_v3` → `serve_v3`), whose wait is `stable_once_durable`. Held to it now: with both candidates
>   stopped a `COMMIT` answers `NFS4ERR_DELAY` after 1.0008–1.0024 s (3 of 3); red-checked with the wait removed, it
>   and a `FILE_SYNC` write answered `NFS4_OK` in 285 and 349 µs. Once the candidates' confirmations lapse, the
>   owner's lease fence (AUD-29-83) answers every call `NFS4ERR_DELAY` at once until a heartbeat after they resume.
> - *A virtio-fs or vhost-user guest's `FSYNC`* (`slates_bridge_virtiofs`'s device holds it, the guest's later chains
>   served meanwhile; `BridgeAccess::durable_owed`/`durability`/`durable`): through `slates vhost-user` with a stand-in
>   VMM on CI's Linux runners, answered `0` in 368–679 µs with both candidates stopped (red, x86_64 and arm64); now `EIO`
>   after 1.0006–1.0017 s, 8 of 8 on each lane, and once in 3 more on x86_64 answered `0` after 1.000358 s, unexplained
>   (that run printed no log line; the flow now prints the log and the hold's counters at that point and requires the
>   hold's refusal). The device's own tests hold both legs on every Unix host: never durable, `EIO` at the bound with a
>   later read published first; durable, `0` at once.
> - *A WinFsp flush* (`FlushFileBuffers` of a handle, held on the mount, `STATUS_UNEXPECTED_IO_ERROR` past the budget),
>   and a *volume* flush, which answered success on WinFsp's thread with no publication at all, now publishes and waits
>   the same way. Three anchored fleet nodes on CI's `windows-latest` (`crates/cli/tests/live_winfsp.rs`): red, the
>   flush succeeded in 995 µs with both candidates suspended; fixed, error 1117 after 1.0010–1.0283 s (3 of 3), success
>   after the resume. Forming that fleet found a Windows defect in the runtime: a UDP socket reported a
>   port-unreachable an earlier send drew as `WSAECONNRESET` on its next `recvfrom`, which ended a fleet serve socket's
>   receive loop at its first probe of a peer still starting (3 of 4 starts never formed). The fix that landed is
>   liveness's (00c4add1, first pushed as d8a8d859: every Windows datagram socket, an adopted one too, made with
>   `SIO_UDP_CONNRESET` and `SIO_UDP_NETRESET` off); the WinFsp flow needs it to form its fleet.
> - *A publication that owed a whole record before the fleet knew the volume* (2026-11-18, g227): every claim above waits
>   for the position `live_ship::durable_target` names, and while the volume's head was unplaced it named the head as
>   it stood, ignoring a whole record owed for a publication that could not become an entry (the credit full with the
>   candidates stopped). With nothing shipped yet a claim waited for nothing; with a head it waited one position short of
>   the record holding its write. The owed record now counts placed or not (`owed_position`, unit-tested red first).
> - *Landings* need no wait: a landing claims what it wrote to disk, which holds it; a takeover that loses the volume's
>   undurable tail serves the disk's bytes through the base, and a later landing that would revert the disk is refused
>   by the witness check.
> Found on the way and handed to live-fixes with the fleet re-formation defects: on Windows, a candidate's anchor kills a
> daemon suspended past the liveness budget and starts a successor under a fresh identity, after which the owner's mount
> stayed fenced and the fleet did not re-form within 40 minutes (CI, 1 run); the flow now suspends each anchor with its
> daemon.

> **Phase one with a candidate that holds no copy (2026-11-05).** Every candidate's report counts toward `f + 1`, an empty
> one too, and every reporter raises its fence to the takeover's epoch, an empty one too: a candidate with no copy makes
> an empty copy fenced at that epoch (`live_ship::fenced_copy`, at the successor's own report and at a remote
> candidate's). Before, the successor counted itself only when it held a copy (a takeover could wait for its quorum for
> good), and a remote candidate's empty report raised no fence, which the nemesis model shows breaks StaleNeverCommits
> (10 seeds; bug record `docs/bugs/2026-11-05-a-live-takeover-counted-no-empty-report-and-fenced-no-empty-copy.md`).
>
> **A live log is durable only once every candidate could open it (2026-11-05, A-92 piece 4c).** A successor opens the
> log through its own copy of the lineage key in the last whole entry, so a write is answered only once that entry
> carries a key for every remote candidate in the neighbourhood and is itself durable (`live_ship::answerable`); a log
> whose whole entry lacks one is checkpointed again once the owner's shard has delivered the missing pair. A sealed head
> waits for the same coverage (`fleet::sealing_covers`). Before, a volume made while a candidate was stopped kept a whole
> entry with no key for it, and that candidate, the successor, never served the volume. A takeover also acts on a
> holder's `ConfigurationStale` now (pages and the adopted record), so a learner successor one version behind fetches
> the configuration rather than asking under it for good (same bug record).
>
> **A candidate is covered only by its current incarnation's acceptance (2026-11-09, A-271).** "A key for every remote
> candidate" above counts a candidate only once this shard's pair to its anchor was accepted by its current member id
> (`live_ship::covered_anchor`): a node replaced at its own anchor (its store destroyed, a new member id) is not covered
> by its predecessor's acceptance, so writes wait until it accepts its redelivered pair, and the whole entry already
> written for the anchor then opens for it. A successor never makes the log's key: it reads only keys recorded here
> (`seal_keys::recorded_lineage`, `recorded_namer`), a sealed log without them is refused `no_key`, and that refusal
> waits for the key by event, bounded by `NO_KEY_WAIT_NS` (A-271 below). The store-destroyed flow on both Linux arches:
> 48 of 48 taken over, the replacement the successor in 26, no key waited for (diag-live-durability-80; BENCHMARKS "A
> live volume taken over by a node replaced at its own anchor"). An owner lost after the replacement is configured and
> before it accepts the owner's pair left the volume unserved while the replacement was its successor: at `f ≥ 2` a
> fellow candidate now hands the replacement the key, wrapped to its recipient (A-295 below); at `f = 1` no survivor can
> adopt the log in that window, since its recorded holders lack the replacement until it is covered, a second failure
> for the volume (GAPS, 2026-11-17).
>
> **Phase one counts among the recorded holders (2026-11-06, A-240).** "Every candidate's report counts" above now
> holds only for a candidate the shipper recorded as a holder. A member placed after the writes still reports and is
> fenced, but does not count toward `f + 1`. Each shipper records its epoch and holders in the volume's catalog and
> ships nothing until that catalog is placed. Phase one waits for `f + 1` of those holders and never falls back to the
> current placement.
>
> **A checkpoint ships a live volume's changes, not the volume (2026-11-05).** A live log's whole record copies every
> byte of the volume; it is owed only when a delta would not apply to what the candidates hold (the log's first record,
> a holder behind the retained tail, a publication that could not be shipped). A shard's local checkpoint is none of
> those: it restarts the recovery journal once the deltas reach the size of the shard's metadata, and it had been mapped
> to a whole record, so one write in three copied the volume (68 of 201 records) and the record behind it was refused
> for credit (431 of 2,395). Now the checkpoint takes each changed live volume's record as a delta publication does
> (`verbs::capture_live_changes`) and ships it once the checkpoint commits, for the volumes the checkpoint carried
> (`live_ship::note_checkpoint`). Held by `a_live_volumes_writes_ship_their_changes_not_the_volume` (red first: 68 whole;
> after: 1, the log's first). Interleaved with main, the stable-write latency is unchanged (BENCHMARKS "What a
> checkpoint shipped"); the whole copies and the credit refusals are gone.
>
> **A candidate's copy stays within its bound (2026-11-06).** A candidate keeps a whole entry and the entries after it,
> within twice the volume's size (`live_ship::hold_bound`). With whole records rare, the copies grew to that bound and
> both candidates refused every entry after it, so no write was durable (at 454 stable 4 KiB writes to a 1 MiB volume:
> `a_long_writer_keeps_the_candidates_copies_within_their_bound`, red first). The owner now counts what a candidate keeps
> (`LiveVolume::kept`) and ships whole once that reaches the volume's size (`kept_reaches_size`): the entry that crosses
> it still fits, since no publication is larger than the volume. After: 768 writes answered, 4 whole records, no
> refusal for the bound.
>
> **A candidate's copy survives its own restart (2026-11-06).** A candidate's copies of live logs were not in its shard's
> recovery image, and it acknowledged an entry before anything was published: after a warm restart (its anchor kept) it
> held nothing it had acknowledged (`a_candidates_copy_survives_its_own_daemons_restart`, red first: head 4 before, none
> after). Now each copy, with its owner, fence and head, rides the held image (`live_ship::HeldLive` in
> `content_holder::HeldImage`), and an entry, an install or a fetch is answered only once the publication carrying it
> commits (`live_ship::acknowledged`), as content and register holders answer; a warm restart holds it again
> (`restore_copies`). The cost is that publication on each acknowledgement, and the held image is rebuilt whole at each
> one, so it grows with what a candidate keeps (up to the volume's size of changes since the last whole entry). An
> earlier form of this change also shipped a whole entry once the changes since the last were as large as it, which kept
> that small (193–196 µs added at the median, p99 513–715 µs, at load 58–107); it is withdrawn, since the install image
> kept beside the log (live-durability) means a whole entry on the log is shipped only at the holder's bound.
>
> **A candidate's copy is charged, against the claim it reserved (2026-11-18, A-401, §4.2).** A copy's entries were heap
> outside every ledger. Now the candidate reserves the volume's claim as it takes the first entry
> (`live_ship::admit_claim`, refused `NoRoom` when it cannot), and the copy is charged against that claim. Only its bytes
> past the claim are charged on the control shard (`live_ship::Room`, `ShardBudget::charge_replicated`), refused
> `NoRoom` when that shard has no room, with the copy left as it was. A dynamic volume's claim holds no bytes, so its
> copy is charged there whole. A destroy's let-go credits the copy and releases its claim at the control shard's next
> reconciliation (`live_ship::reconcile_claims`), which also admits a warm restart's copies' claims again.
>
> **The held image is incremental (2026-11-08, A-270; on main 2026-11-18 at image version 27, delta version 10).** What
> a shard holds for other owners is now keyed pieces: the
> content hold and the mirror records one piece each, one per held register, and of each live copy a head piece and one
> piece per entry, keyed by slot. A delta carries the pieces put and the keys removed since the last publication, so an
> acknowledgement's publication carries the entry it added. Persisting every acknowledged live entry now adds nothing
> that main's own spread can show at the median: 65–79 µs, against main's 65–76 µs and the whole image's 207–225 µs
> (BENCHMARKS). Still carried whole when changed: the content hold's image and the mirror records.
>
> **A held register is a head and its positions (2026-11-18, A-367; image version 29).** A held register was one piece
> holding every position its acceptor kept, and a green's register on its holders is a ledger, never compacted: each
> version's acknowledgement re-encoded and re-wrote every version the holder kept, so a commit at `f > 0` grew by a
> position's bytes a version. Now a register is a head piece (its authority, fence and moved-from owner) and a piece per
> accepted position, keyed by its sequence; a holder's acceptor keeps which positions it accepted or dropped since its
> last committed publication (`Acceptor::tracking_changes`), and a delta carries the head and those positions only. An
> acceptor whose changes do not account for its positions against what was published (one put in place of another) is
> carried whole, as its pieces. Still carried whole when changed: the content hold's image (its every manifest and
> chunk, at each publication that changed it) and the mirror records.
>
> **The content hold is its pieces (2026-11-18, A-376; image version 30).** The content hold's image was one piece,
> every stored chunk, held manifest and stage, re-encoded at every publication and re-put whenever it changed: at
> `f > 0` every version of a green, whose inputs its holders keep. Now each stored chunk, each manifest held for an object
> and each stage is a piece (`ContentHold::pieces`), the hold keeps which it changed since the last committed
> publication (`ContentHold::changed_pieces`), and a delta carries those; a recovery puts them back into the hold's image
> (`ContentHold::image_from_pieces`) and rebuilds the hold from it as before, every chunk verified. Still carried whole
> when changed: the mirror records.
>
> **One lane a holder, only to holders of the catalog, and no session left with a cancelled request (2026-11-07).**
> The dispatch round (`live_ship::dispatch`, `send_from_control`) now ships the way the record plane's sessions allow.
> - *One lane a holder, the holders at once.* A dispatch sent a write's messages to the holders one after another, and
>   folded their answers only once every holder's exchange had ended, so with one candidate stopped every write it
>   carried waited for that candidate's exchange to give up. Now each holder has one lane, a dispatch's lanes run
>   together on the control shard, each lane's answers are folded on the owner as its exchange ends, and a holder whose
>   lane is shipping is sent nothing new until the lane ends (`lane_ended`), then what it lacks: only that holder's, and
>   only when it answered. Sending every holder's let two holders with no link (both stopped) end each other's lanes
>   at the shards' speed, 565,202 unanswered sends in one stop (`both_candidates_stopped_draw_no_storm_of_sends`).
> - *Only to holders of the catalog.* A candidate derives what it keeps of a live log from the volume's catalog, which
>   the record plane places within a record period; an entry sent before was refused
>   (`fleet.live.hold_refused.no_catalog`), and installs drawn by it held the candidate's one session against the record
>   plane's re-ship of that catalog. The owner now ships to the candidates any placement of the catalog named
>   (`catalogued_holders`), kept as a union so a candidate away during one round is not dropped for good, and builds
>   nothing for a holder whose lane is busy (an install clones the whole volume).
> - *No session left with a cancelled request.* An exchange's requests are children of the task that made it, and a
>   task's end cancels its children: a request still in flight when its lane ended was dropped with the holder's
>   session in it, and the slot stayed lent for good, so the owner never shipped that holder again. A lane now waits for
>   its exchange's stragglers to report before it ends (`finish_stragglers`).
> Held by two failing tests in `crates/cli/tests/live_fleet.rs`, run on four trees (CI, release, both Linux arches, 5
> runs each, `diag-live-durability-21`):
> | tree | `each_candidate_stopped_in_turn_holds_no_write_and_catches_up` | `a_new_live_volumes_first_writes_go_only_to_candidates_holding_its_catalog` |
> |---|---|---|
> | main | 0 of 10 (the first write after each stop 406–1,064 ms) | 1 of 10 |
> | one lane a holder | 10 of 10 (2.8–99.5 ms) | 1 of 10 |
> | and only to catalog holders | 10 of 10 | 10 of 10 |
> | and the stragglers' wait | 10 of 10 | 10 of 10 |
> And `both_candidates_stopped_draw_no_storm_of_sends`: main 10 of 10 (30–58 unanswered sends while both are stopped),
> the lanes without the rule above 8 of 10 (565,202 and 555,320 in the two failures), the whole series 10 of 10 (17–42,
> bound 66; `diag-live-durability-24`).
> On KIND (raft-chaos, release, real pods), main stalled with both of the owner's sessions `lent=true` (run
> 42318867890: `wan` at durable 123 of 126, `wan-loss` 199 of 202, `ceiling` 0 of 3). The lanes with the catalogued
> holders alone acknowledged every write in every profile (run 42357764313: `wan` p99 979 ms, max 1.59 s), and so did
> the lanes with the stragglers' wait (run 42326682216: `wan` p99 1.36 s). So KIND does not separate the stragglers'
> wait's own effect. Its failing test is on the simulated fabric, where the mechanism is deterministic:
> `a_lane_that_ends_with_a_holder_unanswered_gets_every_session_back` (`crates/cluster/tests/live.rs`) ships from a task
> of its own with one holder silent, settles (`Stragglers::settle`, which the lane's `finish_stragglers` calls) and ends;
> both sessions come back. With the settle removed, only the answering holder's does ([HostId(2)] against both). The first write's ~99 ms in some runs is a lane waiting one record period for its holder's session,
> lent to the record plane (`ship_head`); open.
>
> **An install image beside the log (2026-11-07).** A holder that falls behind the retained tail is installed with the
> owner's last whole state. If it already holds that state, a newer one is needed. Until now that set `owes_whole`, so
> the next write's record carried the whole volume as an entry to every holder. The up-to-date candidate had to take it
> before any later write was durable, and `durable_target` made every waiting write wait for that record.
>
> The trigger was common because the retained tail's byte bound was the last whole record's size, fixed while the
> volume grew. In the chaos flows (CI, `diag-live-durability-14`, release, both Linux arches) every run made such
> records:
> - 20–45 MB each, each exchange 100–600 ms;
> - the lanes they held turned later writes away for credit, which owed further whole records;
> - writes of 1.2–1.9 s followed.
>
> Now the stale checkpoint sets `owes_image` instead (`LiveVolume::owes_image`), and the log is untouched:
> - the next publication appends its change as usual, and the volume's whole state, which is that publication's
>   state, becomes the install at the head just appended (`live_ship::refresh_image`);
> - on the record period a volume with nothing unpublished makes it the same way, so an idle writer leaves no holder
>   waiting;
> - the retained tail's bound follows the image, so a laggard is sent entries while they cost less than installing the
>   volume as it is now;
> - nothing waits on `owes_image`; only the lagging holder is installed;
> - a log that lost a change (`owes_whole`) still takes a whole record, and an image is never made then, since the
>   volume's state is past its head.
>
> Held by `a_candidate_behind_the_retained_tail_is_installed_without_a_whole_record_on_the_log` (one candidate stopped
> for the middle third of 180 sequential stable writes: one whole record, at least one install, and the candidate caught
> up).
>
> **The period in slices (2026-11-17, g230).** The record period's live work on a shard (following each volume's
> candidates, answering writers whose condition is met, owing or shipping a whole record or image, and re-sending what
> each holder lacks) visited every live volume the shard owned in one turn, so its cost grew with the volumes and every
> client of the shard waited behind it. It now runs a slice of about the shard's step quantum a turn
> (`live_ship::period_slice`, the quantum a destroy's or an archive's slice is cut by), resuming after the last volume
> visited; the first volume of a slice is always visited, so the period always ends. Held by
> `a_shards_live_volumes_are_visited_by_the_period_in_slices_and_none_is_starved` (`crates/server/tests/fleet.rs`: 24
> live volumes, the quantum cut to one volume a slice, every log durable at its head after three periods). Owed
> (measurement): the owner shard's longest step with thousands of live volumes, before and after. Until A-347 the
> slices over the control shard's own volumes ran in one poll (an inline call; `xshard::Turns`, §4.10's A-347 status).
>
> **A holder's return in turns (2026-11-18, A-324, g230).** When a holder's record session is established again, every
> shard sends it what its live volumes owe it at once (`live_ship::holder_reached`). That ran in one turn of each shard:
> every live volume visited, and every message the holder lacked built, an install a copy of the whole volume each. It
> now walks each shard's live volumes in turns of the shard's step quantum, as the period does (`reached_walk` and
> `reached_slice`, one task of the control shard a shard, each turn awaited within the live exchange's budget), each
> turn's messages dispatched before the next; a turn the shard does not answer ends the walk, and the period sends the
> rest. Counted `fleet.live.reached_slices`. Held by `a_holders_return_is_walked_in_turns_and_it_takes_every_log`
> (`crates/server/tests/fleet.rs`: 12 live volumes, a holder held off its shard for two liveness budgets while each is
> written, the turn cut to one volume; at least 12 turns, and the holder at the owner's head on every volume; held again,
> up to four times, until the owner has dialed the holder afresh, since an owner judging its lanes in its own time under
> load need not end the link in one hold: "0 turns for 12 volumes" under a full suite, 2026-11-18). Owed
> (measurement): the owner shard's longest step when a holder of thousands of live volumes returns, before and after.
> Until A-347 the turns over the control shard's own volumes ran in one poll (an inline call; `xshard::Turns`, §4.10's
> A-347 status): the measurer's longest steps of at most 12.0 and 42.0 ms over 1,000 and 4,000 volumes grew with the
> volumes as one poll would (an inference from the scaling, not traced).
>
> **The credit in bytes (2026-11-17, A-200 amended that day, AC-8.9).** The owner's credit was a fixed two entries, and
> a publication past it shipped the whole volume next. Now the entries not yet durable and the retained tail are each
> held to the wire bytes of the whole state an install would send (`slates_db::live::Bounds::of_whole`, set at each whole
> record and install image), so a burst of barriers on one volume ships its deltas at once and the volume is shipped
> whole only where that is the cheaper catch-up. Held by `a_burst_of_writes_to_a_live_volume_ships_its_changes_not_the_volume`
> (`crates/server/tests/fleet.rs`: sixteen clients write half a page each while both holders are held off their shards; every
> write answered, no publication turned away, no whole record; red on the fixed credit) and the byte bounds' unit tests in
> `crates/db/tests/live.rs`. The same day a lane began sending the entries a holder lacks as one batch a congestion window
> (A-200's second amendment of 2026-11-17, `live_ship::take_batch`, `serve_entries`): in the same flow each held holder
> was caught up in batches of several entries an exchange (`fleet.live.batches`, `fleet.live.batched`), where it had
> been sent one entry an exchange.
>
> **A whole state in flight is not counted against the deltas (A-371, 2026-11-18; g230).** The credit counted every entry
> not yet durable, the whole state the owner had just appended among them, and the owner sets the credit from that very
> entry's size: so until a whole entry was durable every delta behind it was refused `NoCredit`, each refusal owed a
> whole state again, and the volume shipped whole once more as soon as the credit freed. The measurer's 32 writers on one
> 128 MiB live volume saw it as two extra whole records of about 135.5 MB in every completed run (1 became 3), each an
> O(volume) build in one turn of the owner shard. A whole state now rides one past the credit as `append_checkpoint`
> always said, and the credit a delta is held to counts the unsettled deltas alone (`Shipper::unsettled_whole_bytes`);
> a whole state is still admitted only while everything in flight is within the credit, so at most the credit's deltas
> and the whole states admitted past it are in flight. Held by `deltas_behind_a_whole_state_in_flight_are_admitted_within_
> the_credit` (`crates/db/tests/live.rs`: a whole state of 64 KiB appended as the daemon appends it, then 4 KiB deltas
> with nothing acknowledged: every delta within the credit admitted, the next refused, no second whole state, all settled
> by the acknowledgement), red with the whole state counted. Owed (measurement): the 32-writer run's whole records and
> step lengths again.
>
> **A whole entry of more than one piece is sealed in turns, and the writes made meanwhile follow it (A-377, 2026-11-18;
> g230).** A live log's whole entry (its first, and every checkpoint) was made and sealed in the one turn of the owner
> shard that published it: the volume's image, every extent read into it, then an AEAD and keyed names a byte, about a
> second a GiB (g251's trace of a taken-over volume's first publication: 1.06 s in one turn). The publication's turn now
> captures the plain body (a memcpy a byte) and begins a build (`live_ship::WholeBuild`): a task of the owner shard seals
> it a piece a turn, a share of the shard's quantum each (`config::wrap_slice_ns`, as A-323's wrap and A-347's open), and
> yields between. Each publication made meanwhile is captured in its own turn and queued behind it, held to the credit
> the whole entry will set. Nothing is appended while it seals; then the whole entry when the credit admits a
> checkpoint, and each queued publication in order as the credit admits it, waiting in its place otherwise and going on
> when an acknowledgement frees the credit or at the record period (`append_ready`). Positions are taken at the append
> in publication order: a barrier made meanwhile waits for the position its entry will take (`durable_target`), and a
> restart's kept position counts the build and its queue (`owned_piece`). A build ends unappended only when its owner is
> superseded (its writers were refused) or its keys are refused; the volume then owes a whole state, and every writer
> waiting past its position waits for it (`fold_waiting_onto`). While a build or its queue holds the chain the record
> period appends what the credit admits and makes nothing beside it, judged before the candidates' keys; and only a
> whole entry pays an owed whole state (`append_entry`), so a queued delta captured before a refusal cannot. Held by
> `a_live_whole_entry_is_sealed_in_turns_and_writes_made_meanwhile_follow_it` (`crates/server/tests/fleet.rs`: a volume
> of 3 MiB, its seal turns cut to a piece each, eight writers and one more write as it goes live): 8 of 8 answered at
